messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?
I want a fair financial share, and I haven’t agreed to A buying the house at a discount. I don’t want to hurt her, but I won’t subsidize her purchase.
Thank you. I’d like to buy the house with my husband at a family discount. I know C hasn’t agreed yet, so we can’t proceed without her.
Thank you. I’d like to see whether my share could give me enough to start a dance studio; that would mean a lot to me. I’m not sure what’s fair or legally possible yet.
Mostly. I want a fair financial share, but I haven’t agreed to A’s discounted purchase. And yes, I don’t want this to damage my relationship with my sisters.
Affordability is part of it. I want my husband and me to build some security of our own. Keeping the house in the family matters too, but it isn’t the whole reason.
That fits. Timing matters to me, though I don’t know what’s possible yet. I’d also hope we can work this out kindly between us.
Yes, that fits. I’m not in a rush, and I don’t want anyone pressured into a decision.
Yes, that fits. I’m comfortable with decisions based on clear facts and no pressure; an independent valuation can inform things, but it doesn’t decide whether a family discount is possible.
I’m a little concerned about how long it might take for my share to become cash. I’d need to understand the likely timing before I could tell whether either option would work for me.

I’m not ready to accept those options or the one-third assumption; the shares and terms aren’t settled. A voluntary discount would need C’s agreement, and I’d want the options discussed without pressure.

The principles seem fair, but don’t assume equal thirds or a right to match—that depends on the will and legal advice. I’m not agreeing to a discount. There’s no real deadline, but we can give B a clear update on the process.
